## Six years of trying this in R and Stan

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
| Package | Since | Stars | CRAN |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `EpiNow2` | 2020 | 141 | 58,073 |
| `epinowcast` | 2021 | 67 | not on CRAN |
| `epidist` | 2023 | 16 | not on CRAN |
| `primarycensored` | 2024 | 9 | 11,294 |
| `baselinenowcast` | 2025 | 10 | 1,678 |

::: {.attribution}
Stars and creation dates from the GitHub API, downloads are CRAN totals
to 2026-08-11 from [cranlogs](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/), retrieved
2026-08-12, and `baselinenowcast` 2026-08-13.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
- All of them are used by public health departments, including CDC,
  UKHSA, RKI, ECDC and WHO
- [`epinowcast`][lk-epinowcast] was the attempt at community developed tools
- In many cases the package is too complex for anyone else to use
- We see fragmentation, and a lot of small mistakes in outbreak
  modelling that add up to real biases
:::
::::
